description: Number of agents in the synthetic city.
notes: Age distribution of Salt Lake County, UT (2025 Census estimates, via multigroup.vaccine), rescaled to n.

description: Number of infections at the start of each simulation (in the latent state).
Basic reproduction number targeted when calibrating the contact matrix.
notes: Below the 12-18 range of Guerra et al. 2017 (Lancet Infect Dis 17(12):e420-e428); the measles package uses 15. Not a model argument: it enters through the calibrated contact matrix.

description: Proportion of the population vaccinated.
Efficacy of two doses of MMR vaccine.
citation: Utah DHHS Measles Disease Plan (updated March 26, 2026) ("~97%")

description: Probability of transmission per contact between an infectious and a susceptible agent.
citation: Assumption: highly transmissible; Utah DHHS Measles Disease Plan (updated March 26, 2026): "90% of susceptible contacts will develop disease"
notes: Fixed high, then the contact matrix is calibrated to R0. Same as the measles package.

description: Average days from exposure to the start of the prodromal (infectious) period.
citation: Utah DHHS Measles Disease Plan (updated March 26, 2026): exposure to prodrome averages 8-12 days

description: Average days of the infectious prodromal period, before rash onset.
citation: Utah DHHS Measles Disease Plan (updated March 26, 2026): prodrome lasts 2-4 days (range 2-8); contagious 4 days before rash onset

description: Average days of the infectious part of the rash period.
citation: Utah DHHS Measles Disease Plan (updated March 26, 2026): contagious to 4 days after rash onset
notes: The measles package uses 3 (infectivity is minimal after day 2 of rash).

description: Reduction in contacts during the rash period (1 = agents with rash stay home).
Probability that a case is hospitalized during the rash period.
notes: Converted to the daily rate that ModelMeaslesMixing() takes. Observed: 8% overall in Utah (Jones et al. 2026, NEJM Evid 5(8)); 18.5% in West Texas (Wang et al. 2026, MMWR 75:252-257). Does not affect shedding or triggers.

description: Average days in hospital.
notes: Observed stays are shorter: a mean of 2.1 nights in Utah (Jones et al. 2026).

description: Number of simulated days.
Day of peak shedding, counted from prodrome onset (4 = rash onset).
citation: Corchis-Scott et al. 2026, Emerg Infect Dis 32(10): shedding during the prodrome and around rash onset

description: Last day of shedding, counted from prodrome onset (about 14 days after rash onset).
citation: Corchis-Scott et al. 2026: urine RNA up to 14 days; CDC: RT-PCR positive up to 10+ days after rash

description: Ratio between the peak and the ends of the shedding profile (log10 scale).
notes: Only sets the shape; the profile is normalized to sum to one.

description: Mean of the log10 total genome copies shed per infection (log-normal).
citation: STOTEN 2024: about 10^8.7 copies per infection per day over about 2 weeks; Corchis-Scott et al. 2026: median 1.4 x 10^11 copies per person per day

description: Standard deviation of the log10 total genome copies shed per infection.
citation: Corchis-Scott et al. 2026: shedding spans four orders of magnitude

description: Wastewater volume per person per day.
Standard deviation of the log-normal measurement error.
Measurements below the LOD are recorded as non-detects (3 log10 copies/L).
Days of the week (t %% 7) when wastewater is sampled: 3 times a week.
notes: Utah samples measles twice a week (Deseret News, March 21, 2026: https://www.deseret.com/lifestyle/2026/03/21/measles-outbreak-utah-public-health-lab-wastewater-surveillance/). Sensitivity: 1, 2, 3, and 5 times a week.

description: Days from sample collection until the result is available to act on.
citation: Assumption, informed by: Utah pilot (2020), transport within 24 h and a 48-h lab turnaround; Provo, UT (2025), 4 days from collection to DHHS notification by WastewaterSCAN; NWSS, a median of 2 days (IQR 1-4) from collection to testing; New Mexico (2025), results within 10 days
notes: The Utah lab figure is from the COVID-19 pilot; measles assays may take longer. Sensitivity: 0, 1, 3, 5, 7, and 10 days.

description: Probability that a case is detected (and reported) during its rash period.
citation: Assumption; Corchis-Scott et al. 2026 estimated 5-10x under-reporting in Ontario

description: Days from rash onset until a detected case is reported.
notes: The measles package assumes 2 days from rash onset to detection.

description: Cumulative reported cases that trigger the intervention.
WW result that triggers the intervention.
notes: The default is a placeholder; the analysis replaces it with the calibrated threshold.

description: Reduction in the non-household contacts of the 5-19 age groups once the intervention starts.
